title: See it before the customer does
scenario: "Last incident we learned about errors from Twitter. I want a dashboard and an alert that would have told us first." — Head of Support
mission: Apply the observability layer, import the dashboard, query the logs with KQL and get an SLO alert e-mail triggered through GitOps.
objectives: Golden signals vs RED vs USE

prerequisites.notes: Traffic needed: run the traffic loop from lab 11.

cost: ≈ US$0.30/day Managed Grafana Essential + ingestion within the 1 GB/day cap.

steps.title: Alert
steps.detail: chaos.errorRate in dev via PR → alert e-mail → revert → resolved.

criteria.text: The portal dashboard exists in Managed Grafana
The error-ratio alert fired and resolved
A saved KQL query returns the injected errors

expectedResult: You learn about errors from the platform, not from customers.

concepts.title: What to measure
concepts.body: *Golden signals*: latency, traffic, errors, saturation. *RED* (rate, errors, duration) fits request-driven services; *USE* (utilisation, saturation, errors) fits resources like nodes and disks.

concepts.title: Percentiles and ratios
concepts.body: Averages hide the slow tail — alert on p95/p99 latency computed from histograms. Alert on the *error ratio* (errors ÷ requests), not on raw counts that grow with traffic.

concepts.title: KQL
concepts.body: Kusto Query Language queries Log Analytics: a table, then piped operators (`where`, `summarize`, `project`, `order by`).

example.title: a KQL query on a different signal
example.body: Count container restarts per pod in the last hour:
example.code:
KubePodInventory
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| summarize restarts = max(ContainerRestartCount) by Name
| order by restarts desc

glossary.def: Target for a service level indicator, e.g. 99.5% of requests succeed.
Allowed failure (100% − SLO) that can be "spent" on change.
Metric that counts observations in buckets, enabling percentiles.

recovery: No data: check the Prometheus data collection rule and ama-metrics pods.
dont: Do not alert on averages for latency
hints: Alerts on ratios beat alerts on counts.

interview.question: How do you avoid alert fatigue while still catching real incidents?

debrief: SLO-based alerts on error ratio and latency percentiles reflect user pain; auto-resolve closes the loop after the revert.

checker.plan: Read-only: az grafana dashboard list, az monitor alert history/activity, Log Analytics query.
